author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Centerville announces 2026 Businesses of the Year
text:
The City of Centerville announced on May 22 the winners of its 2026 Business Awards during its annual Business Breakfast at The Golf Club at Yankee Trace. More than 100 guests attended the event, which recognized businesses and organizations for their investment, partnership, and impact on the community.
The awards highlight the importance of local businesses in building a vibrant and connected community. City officials said that recognizing these contributions helps foster continued growth and collaboration among area organizations.
City Barbeque was named Small Business of the Year. Located at 5 East Franklin Street in Uptown, City Barbeque was recognized for supporting community events such as providing meals for bands during last year’s Summer Concert Series, supporting the Uptown Music Series, and participating in Benham’s Grove Event Center’s grand opening. The business plans to improve its space with grant funding from Centerville Community Improvement Corporation. “For their community spirit, continued investment and dedication to making Uptown a more welcoming and active destination, we are proud to recognize City Barbeque as Small Business of the Year,” city officials said.
The Humane Society of Greater Dayton received Large Business of the Year honors. Their recent efforts include bringing the Furry Skurry event to Stubbs Park in 2023 and opening two locations—Dayton Humane Co. resale shop and MeowZa Cat Boutique—at Cross Pointe Shopping Center. “Through their events, business growth and continued presence in Centerville, the Humane Society of Greater Dayton has shown a strong commitment to economic vitality and community impact,” city officials said.
Washington Township was named Community Partner of the Year for collaborating with Centerville on expanding Town Hall Theatre programming with support from Centerville Arts Commission, assisting with Veterans Memorial Plaza expansion at Stubbs Park in 2025, co-hosting events like the Great American Community Garage Sale in 2026, and launching campaigns celebrating local pride. “Through their leadership, collaboration and commitment to serving residents, Washington Township continues to be a valued partner in building a vibrant and connected community,” city officials said.
City Council members expressed appreciation for business owners at this annual event while reminding them about available resources throughout the year.
